newsitem.title: GERMANY: DTB Bund futures set for gains if 103.00 holds.
newsitem.headline: DTB Bund futures set for gains if 103.00 holds.

text.p: German September DTB Bund futures moved swiftly to conquer the key 103.00 area in early Tuesday trade and will clock up more gains as long as prices can consolidate above this level.
Analysts said the slightly stronger mark, which on Tuesday had dragged itself back up from 7-1/2 year lows reached on Monday, was helping sentiment somewhat.

"People were really worried that the mark would just keep going down and putting more and more pressure on the Bundesbank to maybe do something on the repo," said one Frankfurt trader. "It's good for Bunds to see the mark coming back a bit."
By 0727 GMT, the DTB Bund future was trading 18 basis higher on the day at 103.02, holding relatively comfortably above the 103.00 pivot level. The mark was just over 1.83.

Technical analysts said 103.15 to 103.17 would be the next region for the contract to target, but said that although the mood was slightly better, a move this far might be too ambitious for this session.
"The market is still pretty cautious, and with all the U.S. numbers due people will be reluctant to push things too far," said one.
The U.S. Q2 employment cost index is due at 1230 GMT.

Analysts polled by Reuters expect the index to show a slight rise to 0.8 percent from 0.6 percent previously, but economists in the U.S. warned that a higher-than-expected number would be "big problem" for the market.
If Treasuries were to have problems, Bunds too are likely to come under pressure, traders said.
Analysts at DMG Futures and Options said they were exoecting a 0.7 percent gain the U.S. employment cost index, but said there was a risk that this may already have been discounted in debt markets.
In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark Bund was trading 13 ticks higher at 103.39 by 0748 GMT for a bid yield of 5.535 percent.
The 10-year yield spread to Treasuries was at 69 basis points, a touch tighter than Monday's 70 basis point closing level.
